title: Hare traction splint
stem: Trauma room. Mr Lo, 30, fell from a motorbike. He has an isolated closed mid-shaft fracture of the left femur (confirmed on X-ray): the thigh is swollen, shortened and deformed. He is haemodynamically stable. Apply a Hare traction splint on the model, explaining as you go.

phases.title: Before the splint
phases.goal: Is it indicated? Analgesia and neurovascular status first.

notes:
Checked against manufacturer guidance for the Hare traction splint, JRCALC, and BOAST guidance on femoral shaft fractures.

Indication: isolated closed mid-shaft femoral fracture — traction reduces pain, muscle spasm and bleeding, and improves alignment. Contraindications: pelvic fracture, hip injury, knee injury or proximal tibial fracture, ankle or foot injury on the same leg, partial amputation, and (relative) open fracture with exposed bone ends. Give analgesia first (IV opioid and/or a femoral nerve or fascia iliaca block). Check pulses, motor and sensory function before and after.

Steps: measure against the uninjured leg (ischial tuberosity to about 20 cm beyond the heel); open and position the support straps; apply the ankle hitch; take manual traction; slide the splint under the leg with the ring against the ischial tuberosity; secure the ischial strap; attach the hitch to the traction hook; wind the ratchet to mechanical traction (about 10% of body weight, up to 7 kg / 15 lb, or until pain eases and the leg length is similar); release manual traction; fasten the leg straps (avoiding the knee and fracture); raise the stand; re-check neurovascular status.

Your notes match this, including the 10% body weight up to 7 kg guide.
